evidence: Skill procedure for check 25: 'every prompt opens http://localhost:3000 and directs the judge to the Playwright MCP tool'; defect is 'any prompt that could be satisfied by reading source, memory, or a first paint'. All five prompts satisfy the Verify line on line 1: gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1 and scored/visual/prompt.md:1 each begin 'Evaluate the live Colderwater playground at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP.' Every judge.toml declares the playwright MCP server (line 8-12 in each: command = "playwright-mcp"), so the tool the prompt names exists. Each prompt keeps {app_context} and {criteria}; test.sh:198-200 substitutes the context, and app_context.md:4 repeats the URL. Source: render prompt.md:1 'Use only rendered browser behavior'; constraints prompt.md:1 'Use only rendered browser behavior and the live DOM' and :5 'decide it from the listed DOM facts only, not from file names, bundled library names or how the code looks'; functional prompt.md:20 'do not read implementation files to infer success'; polish prompt.md:17 'do not read implementation files'; visual prompt.md:18 'Do not read implementation files and do not infer behavior from styling'. The one DOM-inspection criterion (cw_custom_document_surface) first requires typing a word and then locating that word in the live DOM, so it is a browser observation of the running page, not a source read. Memory: functional prompt.md:9 and polish prompt.md:9 'A criterion passes only on evidence you gathered yourself in this session for that criterion. If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass'; visual prompt.md:11 'Score from screenshots and the rendered page you observed yourself in this session'; constraints prompt.md:5 'if a step could not be performed say so plainly and fail that criterion rather than assuming it passed'. First paint: the render gate criterion demands click, typing with real key presses, readback and a reload; both constraints criteria need typing or a Save plus storage clear and two reloads; the in-dimension gate in all three scored prompts (line 5) requires 'that text typed into the code editor appears in it'; visual prompt.md:12 requires a ten-line draft, a Run, a double-click selection and a two-second caret watch before any screenshot is scored; I read all 42 functional, 6 polish and 3 visual criteria and each lists actions followed by a readback, none can be decided from the initial screen. Real-input rule ('Use real key presses and clicks; do not dispatch synthetic events or change the app's DOM or state from script') is in render:5, constraints:5, functional:20 and polish:17, with the three script exceptions defined once in app_context.md:26. Weak-app probe: a static shell that paints a convincing workspace fails the render gate (typed word must appear) and the scored in-dimension gates; an app that hard-codes pleasing first-paint content gains nothing because every criterion uses judge-chosen fixture text ('You may choose the exact fixture text', functional prompt.md:23). Conforming-alternative probe: a canvas-drawn editor is not forced into source reading, app_context.md:28 sends the judge to screenshots. Limits, stated plainly: this is a reading of the prompt and criterion text; no configured judge run exists on these bytes, so whether the pinned judge model actually obeys these instructions is not measured here. The hosted run in the evidence index is on an earlier candidate and its exported logs hold no tool-call trace I could inspect (only verdict JSON, plus app-restart.sh.used showing the restart MCP tool was invoked), so it does not confirm browser use for these bytes. The scripted golden results are Playwright scripts, not the judge.
